title: Facilitators and barriers to participation in (digital) outpatient lung sports.
summary: Chronic lung and respiratory diseases, such as chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and bronchial asthma, can significantly impair the physical performance and quality of life of those affected. Implementing exercise, for example in the form of outpatient pulmonary sports, can positively impact the physical, mental, and social health of patients with pulmonary diseases, as well as how they cope with their illness. This study aims to investigate personal factors that may encourage or hinder the uptake and maintenance of exercise, using outpatient pulmonary sports as an example. Furthermore, the study will examine whether these factors differ for digital and on-site implementation.
conditions: Chronic lung diseases, e.g. J44; J45; J84; E84;

interventions.name: Participants in outpatient pulmonary sports take part in digital questionnaire study

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- diagnosed chronic lung and respiratory disease
- participation in outpatient pulmonary sports (in person or digitally)
Exclusion criteria:
If, in the last six months, persons have experienced an acute, serious cardiological issue, neurological, musculoskeletal or psychiatric illness has been diagnosed by a doctor and has since prevented you from actively participating in outpatient pulmonary sports (in person or digitally).
